summary: Ad‑hoc CSV export returns tracehook URLs that 401 when export was queued across retention key rotation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that multiple ad-hoc CSV exports from the Console contain tracehook URLs that return 401 when clicked. The exports were initiated during a period of high load; some exports were queued and completed ~20–40 minutes after request. Exports started normally but links embedded in the CSV appear to use short-lived signing tokens that were rotated by the signing service while the job waited in the export queue.

Impact:
- Customer cannot open trace-linked drilldowns from exported CSVs for a subset (~15%) of export rows.
- Affects security-sensitive enterprise org using long ad-hoc windows and heavy CSV exports.
- Prevents timely investigation into spikes; customer has flagged as business-critical.

Observed behaviour:
- Links in the exported CSV are valid immediately after export creation, but 401 within minutes for queued exports.
- Live dashboard trace links (non-export) work fine.
- Quick exports that bypass queue do not show the issue.

Customer-provided files:
- sample-export-20260309.csv (attached by customer)
- screenshot showing 401 from trace link (attached)
steps_to_reproduce: Login to Console as enterprise org user with tracehook enabled
Open a large ad-hoc query or dashboard and trigger 'Export CSV' with a time window producing >100k rows
When system is at >80% export queue depth (e.g., during peak ingest) allow export job to be queued for >10 minutes
Download produced CSV; click any tracehook URL in the csv. Observe 401 if signing key rotated during queue wait
logs: Export job ids observed in customer sample: export_j-9f2b3, export_j-9f2b4
Console logs (export-service) show queued -> started -> completed timestamps with ~32m queue latency
Auth/Signing service logs show key rotation at 2026-03-09T18:02:00Z and 2026-03-09T18:30:00Z
Nginx logs for tracehook endpoint show 401 for the signed token hash H: 0x7a12abf at 2026-03-09T18:40:14Z
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:12 — Support intake: Customer provided CSV and timestamps. Noted pattern where queued exports are affected, interactive links are not.

03/10 11:03 — SRE (Marco) reproduced in staging by forcing export queue delay; observed signed tokens included in CSV are generated at export creation time and validate against current signing key set at time of click.

03/10 14:20 — Hypothesis: signing tokens embedded in CSV are short TTL (10m) and signed with a rotating key set. If job is queued past TTL or key rotation occurs, token validation fails even if link was correct when created.

03/10 16:45 — Confirmed: export-service currently generates tracehook URLs at time of CSV row rendering (job completion) but uses cached token creation path that can reference an older key identifier in some code paths. Key rotation at 18:30 triggered invalidation for tokens created before rotation but consumed after rotation.
03/11 09:00 — Eng found related PR that changed signing TTL from 60m -> 10m for security (PR #6142). This reduces exposure but increases likelihood of expiration for queued exports.
03/11 12:30 — Queue depth/latency spikes correlate with batch ingest backpressure event (incident INC-20260309-2). Long-tail exports were delayed >30m.
03/12 10:00 — Reproduced locally with signing TTL 10m and forced queue delays; tracehook URLs in exported CSV 401 after TTL expires or immediate post-rotation.
comments: Aisha (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports that this started after last week's platform upgrade. They are on enterprise plan; asking for ETA and workaround.
Marco (SRE) 2026-03-10: I can reproduce in staging by pushing multiple export jobs and stalling workers. Suspect signing TTL + key rotation. Investigating signing service logs.

Jin (Backend Eng) 2026-03-11: Found PR #6142 that shortened token lifetime. Security rationale exists but we didn't account for queued background jobs. Proposing two short-term options: 1) increase export signing TTL when export is created; 2) regenerate signed tokens at job completion time using current key. Will validate tradeoffs.
Aisha (Support) 2026-03-11: Customer asks for immediate workaround. Suggestion to recommend small exports or reduce concurrency? Customer prefers server-side fix.

Marco (SRE) 2026-03-12: Implemented staging patch that regenerates tokens at completion; no security regression in quick review. Need Eng review and security sign-off before prod rollout. Scheduling hotfix deploy window 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC if approved.
Customer (MapleHealth) 2026-03-12: Thanks — would prefer regen-at-completion approach. Can we get a temporary mitigation (docs or automated preflight check) until fix is live?
root_cause: Combination of reduced signing TTL (10 minutes) and export queue latency > TTL during peak ingest. Signing tokens embedded for queued exports were generated with a key that rotated before links were consumed, causing validation failures.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: Support advised customer to split very large exports into smaller windows and to run exports when queue depth is low. Engineering implemented a staging patch that regenerates tracehook signed tokens at job completion using the current signing key (PR #6210). Plan: security review + canary deploy to prod-us-east during low-traffic window on 2026-03-14. Long-term: update export-service to always sign at completion and add a preflight queue-depth warning in Console for exports that are expected to be queued >5m.

Reassess signing TTL policy for background exports; add exception or extend TTL for export tokens — owner: security — due 2026-03-21
Add console preflight warning when export job is likely to be queued based on current queue depth — owner: console-ux — due 2026-03-28
